lens_model: claude-opus-5[1m] (cross-model lane attempted: codex exec -m gpt-5.6-sol -c model_reasoning_effort=xhigh, launched read-only on the int worktree; it was still mid-read at the 25-minute budget and produced no answer, so every finding below is my own, proved with throwaway cells run in the int worktree and then deleted)

findings.what: v5's knowledge block prints no record_id, so all THREE roster tools that take one are unreachable from the model's own context — and one of them shipped working under v4. `renderRetrievedKnowledge`'s line is `- [tier] key = value (trust: X)[ not in effect]` and nothing else. `read_knowledge_source`, `read_knowledge_history` (both NEW) and `ask_knowledge_conflict` (v4's, still rostered) all require `record_id` uuids the model can only have learned from the block. v4's renderer printed `record_id=` deliberately — its own comment says "THE ID IS THE POINT for this lane: ask_knowledge_conflict names rows by record_id, and a run that could see a conflict but not address it could only describe the problem" — and the repoint silently dropped it. The shipped text asserts the opposite in three places the model reads: the schema's describe ("exactly as the client-knowledge block printed it"), the instructions ("Give the `record_id` exactly as the block printed it"), and "USE THEM ON A RECORD THE BLOCK ALREADY NAMED". The cut's headline new capability is therefore documented, tested, rostered, hashed into the bundle digest — and unusable.
findings.evidence: Throwaway cell over a 55-record pack, run in the int worktree and deleted: `v5 sample line: - [core] k_000 = "v0" (trust: asserted)` vs `v4 sample line: - k_000 = "v0" [trust=asserted, source=legacy_client_fact, in force, applies_when={"branch":"KL"}, record_id=11111111-1111-4111-8111-000000000000]`; `v5 has record_id? false | v4 has record_id? true`. `clara.retrieve_knowledge` DOES return the id (0230's records are `clara._knowledge_row_json(r)`, whose first key is `record_id`) — the runtime renderer is where it is lost, and `WorkKnowledgeV5` hands the body only `text`, never the records. The World leg cannot catch it because it supplies the id out of band: `CLARA_V21_RECORD_ID` (tests/chat-turn-v21-e2e.mjs:388, tests/chat-turn-v21-serve.mjs:196,288). No unit cell renders a block and looks for an id (grep of `record_id` over tests/chat-turn-v21-tools.test.mjs: 0 hits).
findings.fix: Restore the marks in `recordLine`: `record_id`, and with it the `in force` / firm-scope / `applies_when` marks v19 and v4 both carried (see ADV-S-5). The closure is not deployed yet, so this is a re-measure of the frozen manifest, not a v6. If instead the ids are deliberately withheld, drop the two new tools from the roster and delete the three sentences that promise them.

findings.what: The two inspection reads leave NO durable record anywhere, and the mandatory `reason` they collect is discarded. `input.reason` is never referenced after zod parses it — it is not an argument of either door (both take `(p_firm, p_client, p_record)` only), it is not written to `clara.work_knowledge_reads` (`recordWorkKnowledgeRead` is called from `loadWorkKnowledgeStepV5` and nowhere else), it reaches no trace row, and the reads mint no part. So the field whose existence the header justifies as "a run that must SAY why it is reading a record is a run whose reads a person can account for afterwards" is collected from the model and thrown away. The capability id `accounting_work.inspect_knowledge_source` is registered `modelBound: true` — an egress event, a dispatch authorization owed — and is recorded on zero rows. The in-file comment claims the durable record is "`clara.work_knowledge_reads` plus the tool's own answer in the transcript": the relation holds only the preload, and the segment's parts (impl:851-868) are `text` / `refusal` / status, so the answer survives only inside the in-memory message array.
findings.evidence: `grep -n "input.reason" packages/runtime/workflows/claraWork.v5.tools.ts` → no hits (only `classification.reason` at :260 and :345). `grep -n capabilityId packages/runtime/workflows/claraWork.v5.impl.ts` → 386/529/599/769/833/888/905/984, i.e. `accounting_work.model_segment`, `.retrieve_knowledge`, `.ask_question`, `.record_journal_entry`, `.settle` — `accounting_work.inspect_knowledge_source` appears in no traceRow call. 0230:451-486 / :493-518 show both doors take three arguments and store nothing.
findings.fix: Record each inspection read: either a `clara.work_knowledge_reads` row naming the record's key and the stated reason, or a per-tool-call trace row under `accounting_work.inspect_knowledge_source`. If neither is affordable this wave, drop `reason` from the schema rather than ask the model for an accountability the estate discards.

findings.what: The drift read taken on the resume AFTER THE LAST SEGMENT writes its trace row at exactly SETTLE_TRACE_SEQ, and the settle's own row is then silently dropped. The loop is `for (; segment < budgets.segments; segment++)`, so `segment` reaches `budgets.segments - 1` = 3; the question branch calls `readKnowledgeDriftStepV5(..., segmentTraceBase(segment + 1))` = `segmentTraceBase(4)` = `3 + 4*4` = 19, which IS `SETTLE_TRACE_SEQ` (`3 + budgets.segments*4`). The run then leaves the loop and settles `failed`/`limit` (segments), and `clara.record_work_execution_trace` ends with `on conflict (work_id, run_id, seq) do nothing`, returning the existing id. Both writers swallow the result, so `work_execution_traces` seq 19 holds a drift `tool_call` row and the run's settle — outcome, refusal, receipt — is absent from the trace with no error anywhere. The same collision swallows the settle on the replan-exhaustion arm at :402-407. The cell that should have caught it names the exact property in its comment ("the DRIFT row of segment n+1 is what the body writes on a resume, so it must be inside the scheme rather than past it") and then asserts a different one: it loops `i < B.segments` and checks `segmentTraceBase(B.segments - 1) + 3 < SETTLE_TRACE_SEQ`, never `segmentTraceBase(B.segments)`.
findings.evidence: Throwaway cell (deleted): `segments = 4 | SETTLE_TRACE_SEQ = 19 | drift seq after last segment = 19`, assertion `notEqual(19, 19)` failed. 0195 §9's insert: `on conflict (work_id, run_id, seq) do nothing returning id into v_id; if v_id is null then select t.id ...` — a duplicate seq is a no-op that reports success.
findings.fix: Take the drift only when `segment + 1 < budgets.segments` (a resume that cannot re-enter a segment has nothing to re-plan with), or give the drift its own seq band below the segment block. Widen the cell's loop to `i <= B.segments` so the row the body can actually write is the one the census covers.

findings.what: The new bundle digest is blind to zod refinements, and the one roster schema that carries one is `ask_question` — the exact tool #791's finding named. `z.toJSONSchema` erases `.superRefine` / `.refine` entirely, so `workQuestionFieldSchema`'s rule ("`options` is required for `choice` and forbidden for everything else") contributes nothing to the hashed text. A later `claraWork_v6` that relaxes or removes that rule — changing what the model may send and what `clara.open_work_question` will then be handed — ships under an unchanged digest with an unchanged name, which is verbatim the defect §2 says this cut closed ("`ask_question`'s schema changed between v1 and v2 and the only trace it left was a hand-bumped `tools.id`"). The header's claim "A tool that tightens a bound, adds a field, drops `.strict()`, re-words a `.describe()` the model reads, or is repointed at a different verb now MOVES THE DIGEST. No hand-bumped id, no reviewer's memory, no trust required" is true for each item it lists and false as a general statement; the cell that proves the coverage (§2's "tightens one bound on one schema") exercises `minLength`, which zod does render.
findings.evidence: Throwaway cell (deleted), rebuilding claraWork.v3.tools.ts:103-120 with and without the superRefine: `with superRefine === SAME JSON Schema`, and the two schemas differ at parse time — `{kind:'text', options:[2 options]}` is rejected by one and accepted by the other. The live hashed schema carries no trace of it: `live ask_question hashed schema mentions if/then/allOf/dependencies? false`. Same probe showed `.strict()` vs loose DOES move it (`additionalProperties:false` present/absent) and `.trim()` does NOT (identical output) — so the erasure is specific to checks, not general.
findings.fix: Add a cell that refuses any roster schema carrying a JSON-Schema-unrepresentable check (walk the zod def for `checks`/`refinements` and fail the bundle build, as `toolSchemasJson` already fails on a missing schema), or hash a structural signature of the zod object beside the JSON Schema. Either way soften §2's and the header's claim to name what the digest covers and what it still cannot see.

findings.what: The block DOES shrink at the repoint, and the durable read-set row over-reports what the run saw. Three separate over-claims. (a) `CLIENT_BASIS_LIMIT = 60` is justified as "v19's own record cap, so the block does not shrink at the repoint", but `renderRetrievedKnowledge` prints `records.slice(0, RETRIEVED_MAX_RECORDS)` = 40 and clips each value at 200 chars, where v19 printed up to 60 and clipped at 300. (b) 0230 caps only the REMAINDER at `p_limit`; core and requested are UNBOUNDED (its own comment: "core unbounded, requested unbounded, remainder capped at p_limit 1..200"), so the door can hand back far more than 40 and the print cap can drop CORE rows — the tier the whole terminal exists to protect. (c) `records_shown` and `truncated` describe the DOOR's answer, not the block: `recordWorkKnowledgeRead` writes `p_records_shown = a.records.length` and `p_truncated = a.truncated`, and `completedResultV5` puts the same pair on the Work's durable `result`. A run handed 55 records and shown 40 records a row saying 55 shown, not truncated, status `ok`. The chat block also loses the `in force` (authoritative / legacy-fact) marker v19 added precisely "so the model is told which row governs rather than left to rank two rows of the same key by itself", plus `source_kind`, the firm-default scope mark and `applies_when` — and `retrieve_knowledge` still unions the legacy rows without consulting knowledge_records, so both can appear under one key with nothing saying which is in force.
findings.evidence: Throwaway cell (deleted) over a 55-record pack: `v5 printed lines: 40 | v4(work) printed: 40 | v19(chat) printed: 55`; `v5 has 'in force'? false | v19 has 'in force'? true`; `v5 has applies_when? false | v19 has applies_when? true`. chatTurn.v19.prompt.ts:141 `KNOWLEDGE_CONTEXT_MAX_RECORDS = 60`, :145 `..._VALUE_CHARS = 300`; knowledge-retrieval.mjs:74-75 `RETRIEVED_MAX_RECORDS = 40`, `RETRIEVED_MAX_VALUE_CHARS = 200`. The cell at chat-turn-v21-tools.test.mjs:430 asserts the ASK (`CLIENT_BASIS_LIMIT === 60`) and carries the false sentence as its own message; no cell renders a block larger than the print cap.
findings.fix: Make the print cap the lane's own ask (pass it in, or raise `RETRIEVED_MAX_RECORDS` to 200 with the door's bound as the real wall), restore the 300-char value clip, restore the `in force` / scope / `applies_when` marks, and derive `records_shown` from what the block actually printed so the read-set row answers "what did Clara see" rather than "what did the door return".

findings.where: packages/runtime/workflows/chatTurn.v21.tools.ts:213-232 and :234-258; packages/runtime/workflows/chatTurn.v21.ts:50-61; packages/runtime/workflows/registry.ts (the two new deploy-order paragraphs); packages/runtime/workflows/chatTurn.v11.tools.ts:80-110
findings.what: The deploy-order runbook line is false: a missing migration hands the model the raw Postgres function signature, not `internal`. `authoringRefusal` returns `{ok:false, ...}` unconditionally, so the guard `if (refused.ok === true) return {code:'internal', ...}` in both new mappers is dead code and its comment ("`authoringRefusal` answers `{ok:true}` for an error it does not recognise as a governed refusal") is wrong. Three headers rely on it — chatTurn.v21.ts:55-58, registry.ts twice — all saying "each tool raises `undefined_function` (42883), which `authoringRefusal` does not classify as a governed refusal, so the tool answers `internal` and the turn continues: CONTAINED". The turn does continue, so the containment claim survives; what the tool actually returns is `code:"42883"` with Postgres's own text. The pattern is carried from chatTurn.v19.tools.ts:290 and v20.tools.ts:167, so this cut inherited the bug — but it restates the false sentence as an operator-facing runbook line for two new doors.
findings.evidence: Throwaway cell (deleted): `authoringRefusal(42883) = {"ok":false,"code":"42883","reason":null,"fix":null,"message":"function clara.admit_trade_invoice_work(uuid, uuid, text, text, jsonb, jsonb, text, jsonb, text) does not exist","details":{}}` and `authoringRefusal(ECONNRESET) = {"ok":false,"code":"ECONNRESET",...}`. chatTurn.v11.tools.ts:109 is the single `return { ok: false, ... }`.
findings.fix: Classify on the SQLSTATE in the two new mappers — `/^CLR\d{2}$/` on `refused.code`, the test `knowledge-retrieval.mjs:95-97` already uses — and fall to `internal` otherwise; correct the three headers to say what actually reaches the model.

findings.what: `start_trade_invoice_work` has no in-flight arm, and its sibling in the same file does. 0225 raises CLR13 `operation_in_flight` ("this operation identity is held by an in-flight sibling") when the intent key is held by a call still running; `TRADE_INVOICE_REFUSALS` carries no such token, so the sentence falls through to the door's own engineer-facing text. `run_depreciation_period_for_client` answers the same situation as `ok:true, in_flight:true, periods_run:0` with a sentence a person can read, and the file's header argues at length for doing exactly that ("a refusal nobody reviewed is how a wall becomes a rumour"). Two tools in one file answer the same concurrency fact two different ways.
findings.evidence: `grep -o '\"reason\":\"[a-z_]*\"' packages/db/migrations/0225_trade_invoices.sql` lists `operation_in_flight`; it is absent from the eighteen-token map. The catch at chatTurn.v21.tools.ts:350 routes it through `tradeInvoiceRefusalFromError`, whose fallback is `refused.message`.
findings.fix: Add `operation_in_flight` to `TRADE_INVOICE_REFUSALS` with the depreciation lane's sentence ("a submission under this same request is already in progress; look again in a moment"), or give the tool the same explicit in-flight arm.

findings.what: The floor sentence points a human at a SQL verb. `floorSentence()` ends "A bookkeeper can still run an earlier month by hand through clara.run_depreciation_manual", and DEPRECIATION_CHAT_GUIDANCE repeats the name. The model is instructed to pass that on. A bookkeeper cannot call a database function; the product surface that does exists and is not named.
findings.evidence: apps/web/lib/registers/depreciation.ts:161-175 posts to `/rpc/run_depreciation_manual`, driven by apps/web/components/registers/fa-depreciation-runs-panel.tsx — so the human path is the Fixed assets depreciation-runs panel, not the verb. chat-turn-v21-tools.test.mjs:339 asserts `/clara\.run_depreciation_manual/` against the sentence, so the SQL name is deliberately pinned into model-facing prose.
findings.fix: Name the panel in the sentence and keep the verb in a code comment; repoint the cell to assert the human path instead of the function name.

findings.what: A firm-level (no client) conversation is told a read failed when none was attempted. The step short-circuits to `{status:'unavailable', reason:'no_client'}` and the renderer has one unavailable branch, so the block reads "Client knowledge: the read did not succeed (no_client). This is a READ THAT DID NOT SUCCEED, not a client with nothing recorded. Do NOT tell anybody that this client has no recorded knowledge." The step's own header promises the opposite — "it is also not 'this client has nothing', and the block says which" — and the block does not say which. On a Home conversation this makes the model hedge about a client that does not exist.
findings.evidence: Throwaway cell (deleted) printing `renderRetrievedKnowledge({status:'unavailable', reason:'no_client', records: []})` reproduced that text verbatim. The renderer's only branch on reason is `faceStatusOf`'s `refused` → `denied`; `no_client` shares the generic failure sentence with `read_failed` and `malformed`.
findings.fix: Give `no_client` its own sentence in `renderRetrievedKnowledge` ("this conversation is not about a client, so there is no client knowledge to read"), or have the chat step return an empty-text basis for a Home turn.

findings.what: The drift read is traced under a capability whose declared scope does not name its door, and the leg's new "by capability" lookup is already ambiguous. `readKnowledgeDriftStepV5` writes `capabilityId: "accounting_work.retrieve_knowledge"` while calling `clara.work_knowledge_drift_for`; the v2 entry's scope reads "clara_runtime → clara.retrieve_knowledge (+ clara.record_work_knowledge_read)". So a run with a resume has two `tool_call` rows carrying one capability id, and `rowsA.find(r => r.capability_id === 'accounting_work.retrieve_knowledge')` — the discipline 956ae8bb introduced to replace `find(phase === 'tool_call')` — cannot tell the preload from the drift. The same leg's `deepEqual(afterDispatches.slice(0, -3), ['tool_call'])` re-pins the count of rows ahead of the segment to exactly one, which the comment two lines above says it is deliberately not doing, and which a drift row breaks.
findings.evidence: capabilityId call sites in claraWork.v5.impl.ts: 386, 529, 599, 769, 833, 888, 905, 984 — :529 (preload) and :599 (drift) are the same string. capability-registry-v2.mjs:57 `scope: "clara_runtime → clara.retrieve_knowledge (+ clara.record_work_knowledge_read)"`.
findings.fix: Either add a third v2 id for the drift read or widen the entry's scope string to name `clara.work_knowledge_drift_for`; and make the leg's suffix assertion tolerate an extra knowledge row rather than pin one.

findings.what: The intent key is taken over the MODEL's output, so "a replayed step re-reserves rather than admitting a second Work" holds only when the re-executed model emits a byte-identical payload. `stableOpKey(ctx.taskId, TOOL, input)` canonicalises the tool input; `runModelSegmentStepV21` is a `"use step"` whose `checkpointStep` runs AFTER it returns, so a crash between the door's commit and the checkpoint re-executes the model. A re-sampled call with a differently-worded `memo` — or any other field the model re-phrases — mints a different key and the door admits a SECOND trade-invoice Work for one human request. The leg's correction in §7.1.3 fixed the adjacent mistake (two turns are two requests) and the wider claim was never re-measured.
findings.evidence: chatTurn.v21.ts:153-154 calls `runModelSegmentStepV21` then `checkpointStep`. `canonicalJson` sorts keys and drops `undefined`, so the key is stable against ordering but not against content. trade-invoice-basis.ts:411-413 states the claim ("so a re-run turn resolves to the Work it already admitted instead of admitting a second one"). Carried from v18's `start_journal_work`; not introduced here.
findings.fix: Soften the stanza to name what the key guarantees (idempotence of a replayed CALL, not of a re-sampled segment), or derive the key from a turn-stable identity (task + tool + an ordinal) so a re-executed segment re-reserves whatever the model re-writes.

findings.what: Two small contradictions between comment and code. (a) `read_seq` is documented as "the `work_knowledge_reads` seq this attempt's facts actually landed on"; when all four seqs answer `replayed:true, payload_match:false` the loop exits with `seq = 5` and `landedSeq = min(5, 4) = 4`, so the answer claims seq 4 holds this attempt's facts when it does not. (b) `runKnowledgeRead`'s header says "IT SPENDS budget.toolCalls AND IT NEVER SETS A TERMINAL", and nine lines later the budget-exhaustion arm sets `ledger.terminal = { kind: "budget_exhausted", detail: "toolCalls" }`.
findings.evidence: impl.ts:515 `for (; seq <= KNOWLEDGE_READ_MAX_SEQ; seq += 1)` with `KNOWLEDGE_READ_MAX_SEQ = 4` (:308); tools.ts:220 sets the terminal inside the function whose header denies it.
findings.fix: Return `recorded_divergent: true` (or null `read_seq`) when the bound is reached, and narrow the tools.ts sentence to "a read that REFUSES never sets a terminal".
